title: Lipschitz invariance estimate
statement:
There is a constant $K>0$ such that the following holds. Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let $(\Omega,\mu)$ and $(\Xi,\nu)$ be probability spaces, and let $F$ be a multilinear coefficient family of degree at most $k$ whose Boolean-cube evaluation has variance at most $1$. For $\varepsilon\ge0$, suppose every coordinate influence is at most $\varepsilon$. Let $X$ and $Y$ be independent coordinate families on the respective spaces, each coordinate satisfying the fourth-order invariance moment conditions. For any $c\ge0$ and any $c$-Lipschitz function $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$,
\[
\left|\mathbb E_\mu\psi(F(X))-\mathbb E_\nu\psi(F(Y))\right|
\le Kc\,2^k\varepsilon^{1/4}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: $\mu,\nu$ are probability measures on measurable spaces
$F$ is a coefficient family of degree at most $k$
the Boolean-cube evaluation of $F$ has variance at most $1$
every coordinate influence of the Boolean-cube evaluation is at most $\varepsilon$
the coordinates of $X$ and $Y$ are independent under their respective measures
each coordinate of $X$ and $Y$ satisfies the fourth-order invariance moment conditions
